memories.title: Use httpx.NewClient; http.DefaultClient has no timeout
memories.content: Outbound HTTP uses httpx.NewClient from internal/httpx, which sets a 10 s timeout and the retry policy. http.DefaultClient has no timeout and once left workers hanging for hours.
memories.keywords: http client timeout defaultclient hang

memories.title: Plain Go modules without vendoring
memories.content: Dependencies are plain Go modules with no vendor/ directory. Run `go mod tidy` and commit the go.sum changes together with the code.
memories.keywords: go mod tidy go.sum vendor dependencies modules

memories.title: Worker memory growth is probably the Avro decoder cache (unconfirmed)
memories.content: The slow memory growth of ingest workers over a week is probably the unbounded Avro decoder cache keyed by schema id. Nobody has taken a heap profile yet, so treat this as a hypothesis.
memories.keywords: memory leak growth heap avro decoder cache pprof

memories.title: Partner amounts are normalized to minor units
memories.content: Adapters convert partner price fields from decimal strings into integer minor units plus an ISO 4217 code before building the event. Floats are never used while parsing amounts.
memories.value_text: integer minor units with an ISO currency
memories.keywords: amount price currency minor units decimal parsing adapter

memories.title: Canonical events are BookingCreated, BookingModified and BookingCancelled
memories.content: Adapters map every partner payload to one of three canonical types: BookingCreated, BookingModified or BookingCancelled. Partner-specific statuses such as tentative holds are dropped.
memories.keywords: canonical event types booking created modified cancelled mapping

memories.title: Raw events are kept for 25 months
memories.content: A table TTL drops raw events 25 months after their event date, while aggregated tables keep their data indefinitely. Extending the TTL needs a decision record.
memories.keywords: retention ttl raw events months aggregated tables

memories.title: Occupancy is aggregated by the daily_occupancy materialized view
memories.content: The daily_occupancy materialized view aggregates booked nights per property and day as events arrive. Dashboards must query it instead of scanning raw events.
memories.keywords: materialized view occupancy aggregate dashboard nights property

memories.title: Partner OAuth tokens come from the platform token service
memories.content: Partner OAuth tokens are refreshed by the platform token service; adapters ask it for a valid token before each poll. Adapters never cache tokens themselves.
memories.keywords: oauth token partner credentials refresh adapter poll

memories.title: Partners without webhooks are polled every two minutes
memories.content: Channel managers that cannot push webhooks are polled every two minutes with an updated_since cursor stored per tenant. The cursor only advances after the polled batch has been published.
memories.value_text: every two minutes with an updated_since cursor
memories.keywords: polling partner cursor updated_since webhook tenant

memories.title: Partner webhooks are received by the receiver service
memories.content: Partners that push webhooks call the receiver started from cmd/receiver; internal/receiver checks the HMAC signature and publishes the untouched payload. Parsing happens later in the consumer.
memories.value_text: receiver checks HMAC and publishes raw payloads
memories.keywords: webhook receiver hmac signature partner push payload

memories.title: Messages carry a schema id prefix before the Avro body
memories.content: Every message starts with a magic byte and a four-byte schema id, followed by the Avro body. Tools that read a topic must strip that prefix before decoding.
memories.value_text: magic byte and schema id prefix
memories.keywords: wire format magic byte schema id avro decoding

memories.title: Topic names follow domain.entity.vN
memories.content: New topics are named <domain>.<entity>.v<N>, for example availability.rates.v1. The version number changes only with an incompatible schema.
memories.keywords: kafka topic naming version convention

memories.title: Each assigned partition gets its own goroutine
memories.content: A consumer worker runs one processing goroutine per assigned partition. Running more replicas than there are partitions leaves the extra workers idle.
memories.keywords: consumer goroutine partition replicas workers concurrency

memories.title: Consumers use the cooperative-sticky assignor
memories.content: The consumer group uses the cooperative-sticky partition assignor, so a rolling deploy moves only the partitions of the restarted worker. The eager assignor used to stop every consumer during a rebalance.
memories.keywords: rebalance assignor cooperative sticky consumer group deploy

memories.title: Health probes listen on :8081
memories.content: Workers serve /healthz and /readyz on port 8081, and readiness turns false while a rebalance is in progress. The container probes use these paths.
memories.keywords: health readiness liveness probe port rebalance

memories.title: Profile a worker through pprof on port 6060
memories.content: Workers expose net/http/pprof on localhost:6060 only. From inside the container, run `go tool pprof http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/heap`, and never expose the port through the service.
memories.keywords: pprof profiling heap cpu port debug

memories.title: Each polled batch is traced with OpenTelemetry
memories.content: The consumer starts one OpenTelemetry span per polled batch and links the spans of the messages in it. Trace context from partner webhooks travels in message headers.
memories.keywords: tracing opentelemetry span batch headers context

memories.title: The Ingest Overview dashboard shows lag, throughput and errors
memories.content: Grafana's Ingest Overview dashboard shows consumer lag, events per second per partner and parse errors. Its panel queries are versioned as JSON in deploy/dashboards.
memories.keywords: grafana dashboard lag throughput errors panels

memories.title: Critical pipeline alerts page the on-call rotation
memories.content: Critical pipeline alerts page the on-call rotation through PagerDuty, while warnings only go to the #ingest-alerts channel. Every alert links its runbook in the annotations.
memories.value_text: PagerDuty for critical, channel for warnings
memories.keywords: alerts paging on-call routing runbook channel

memories.title: Lag runbook: check insert latency before scaling
memories.content: When consumer lag grows, first check the insert latency panel; if inserts are slow, adding consumers only adds pressure. Scale replicas only when inserts are fast and lag still grows.
memories.keywords: lag runbook insert latency scale replicas

memories.title: Every ClickHouse table sorts by tenant_id first
memories.content: Every ClickHouse table puts tenant_id first in its ORDER BY, so per-tenant queries read a narrow range. Dashboard queries without a tenant_id filter are rejected by the query proxy.
memories.keywords: tenant_id order by sorting key query filter

memories.title: Property names come from a dictionary, not from event rows
memories.content: Property names and countries are looked up through the properties dictionary, refreshed every five minutes from the platform database. Do not copy them into event rows.
memories.keywords: dictionary property names country lookup dimension

memories.title: Regenerate Go types from Avro with make gen-avro
memories.content: Go structs for the Avro schemas are generated into internal/avro/gen with `make gen-avro`. The generated files are committed, and CI fails when they differ from the schemas.
memories.keywords: avro codegen generate go structs schemas

memories.title: Events with impossible stays are rejected
memories.content: The validator rejects events whose check-out is not after check-in or whose stay is longer than 365 nights. Such events are counted as validation failures.
memories.value_text: check-out after check-in, at most 365 nights
memories.keywords: validation check-in check-out stay nights reject

memories.title: Images are built with ko on distroless
memories.content: Container images are built with ko on top of gcr.io/distroless/static, so the image has no shell and no package manager.
memories.keywords: container image ko distroless build shell

memories.title: The platform database is read only through its replica
memories.content: Lookups against the platform database use its read replica with the ingest_ro role. The pipeline never writes to the platform database.
memories.keywords: platform database replica read-only role lookup

memories.title: Tests are table-driven with named cases
memories.content: The team prefers table-driven tests with a name field and t.Run per case, plus t.Parallel when a case shares no state.
memories.keywords: table driven tests t.Run cases parallel

memories.title: Interfaces are declared where they are used
memories.content: The team prefers small interfaces declared in the package that consumes them, not next to the implementation. Packages export concrete types.
memories.keywords: interface consumer package abstraction concrete types

memories.title: Package names are short lowercase nouns
memories.content: Package names are short lowercase nouns such as parse or sink; util, common and helpers packages are not accepted.
memories.keywords: package naming util helpers lowercase

memories.title: Parsing code receives the current time instead of reading the clock
memories.content: Functions in internal/parse and internal/sink receive the current time as a parameter; only the worker's main loop reads the system clock. Tests pass a fixed time.
memories.value_text: time passed in as a parameter
memories.keywords: time now clock injection parse tests fixed

memories.title: No package-level mutable state
memories.content: Packages hold no mutable package-level variables; dependencies are passed through constructors. The registered Prometheus collectors are the only exception.
memories.keywords: global state package variables constructor dependencies

memories.title: Producers use acks=all, lz4 and a 20 ms linger
memories.content: Every Kafka producer sets acks=all, lz4 compression and linger.ms=20. Changing these settings needs a decision record.
memories.keywords: kafka producer acks compression linger settings

memories.title: Every message carries tenant and partner headers
memories.content: Producers set the x-tenant and x-partner headers on every message, and consumers route by them without decoding the body. A message without them is a producer bug.
memories.keywords: kafka headers tenant partner routing message

memories.title: 2026-01 incident: occupancy charts used the receive time
memories.content: In January 2026 occupancy charts showed bookings on the wrong day because the pipeline stored the time it received each event instead of the partner's event time. Events now carry both, and aggregates use the partner time.
memories.value_text: aggregates use the partner event time
memories.keywords: incident event time receive time occupancy wrong day

memories.title: 2026-07 incident: a schema version stopped the consumers
memories.content: In July 2026 a producer registered a schema version that removed a union branch, and every consumer failed to decode new messages for 40 minutes. A registry compatibility check now runs in CI before any registration.
memories.value_text: compatibility check in CI before registration
memories.keywords: incident schema registry compatibility decode failure consumers

memories.title: Slow worker start-up is probably the schema warm-up (unconfirmed)
memories.content: New workers take about 90 seconds before they consume, probably because they fetch every schema version from the registry at start-up. This has not been measured.
memories.keywords: startup slow schema registry warm up worker hypothesis

memories.title: Create topics through infra/kafka/topics.tf
memories.content: New topics are declared in infra/kafka/topics.tf with their partition count and retention and applied by the infra pipeline. Producers never create topics on the fly.
memories.keywords: topic create terraform partitions retention infra

memories.title: Query local ClickHouse data in the play UI
memories.content: The local ClickHouse answers SQL in its play UI at http://localhost:8123/play with the default user. Use it to check what a local run wrote.
memories.keywords: clickhouse local query play ui sql

memories.title: Try adapters against the partner sandbox tenants
memories.content: Each partner offers a sandbox account wired to the tenant named sandbox-<partner>. Run `make poll-once TENANT=sandbox-<partner>` to fetch one batch and print the raw payloads.
memories.keywords: sandbox partner tenant adapter payload poll once

memories.title: Reproduce a parse error from one raw message
memories.content: To debug a parse error, dump the raw message at its offset with kcat and run `make parse-file FILE=<path>`. It prints the canonical event or the exact parse error.
memories.keywords: debug parse error raw message kcat reproduce

memories.title: One partner still sends XML payloads
memories.content: All partners send JSON except one, whose XML payloads are converted to JSON inside its adapter before mapping. The XML parser rejects DTDs to prevent entity expansion.
memories.keywords: xml json payload format adapter dtd parser

memories.title: The pipeline serves about 1,800 tenants
memories.content: As of October 2026 the pipeline ingests events for about 1,800 tenants and 40,000 properties, peaking at 900 events per second on Saturday mornings.
memories.value_text: about 1,800 tenants, 900 events per second peak
memories.keywords: scale tenants properties events per second peak

memories.title: Events must be queryable within two minutes
memories.content: The freshness target is two minutes from the partner's event time to a queryable row for 99% of events. The freshness panel tracks it per partner.
memories.keywords: freshness target sla latency queryable minutes

memories.title: Enums are typed string constants generated with enumer
memories.content: Enumerations are typed string constants with String and Parse methods generated by enumer. Partner status strings are compared only inside their own adapter.
memories.keywords: enum typed constants enumer string parse status

memories.title: Event log lines carry tenant, partner and event_id
memories.content: The team prefers every log line about an event to carry the tenant, partner and event_id attributes, so one query finds the whole history of an event. Messages themselves stay short.
memories.keywords: log attributes tenant partner event_id fields

memories.title: ClickHouse queries use bound parameters
memories.content: Queries sent to ClickHouse use bound parameters through the driver; building SQL with fmt.Sprintf is rejected because tenant-controlled values reach the query.
memories.keywords: sql parameters injection sprintf query driver

memories.title: Packages that start goroutines check for leaks
memories.content: Every package that starts goroutines calls goleak.VerifyTestMain in its TestMain, so a leaked goroutine fails that package's tests.
memories.keywords: goroutine leak goleak testmain tests

memories.title: 2026-08 incident: catch-up after a partner outage got us throttled
memories.content: After a six-hour partner outage in August 2026, catch-up polling fetched everything at once and the partner throttled all of our tenants. Catch-up now fetches at most three pages per poll.
memories.value_text: at most three pages per poll
memories.keywords: incident partner outage catch up polling throttle

memories.title: The ClickHouse cluster has three shards with two replicas each
memories.content: The analytics ClickHouse cluster runs three shards with two replicas each, and Distributed tables fan queries out across the shards.
memories.keywords: clickhouse cluster shards replicas distributed tables

memories.title: Pull requests stay under about 300 changed lines
memories.content: The team prefers pull requests under about 300 changed lines; larger changes are split and land behind a disabled code path.
memories.keywords: pull request size small split review lines

memories.title: Dashboard queries are capped at 30 seconds
memories.content: The query proxy kills dashboard queries after 30 seconds or 10 GB of memory. Heavy analyses run as scheduled jobs instead.
memories.keywords: query timeout dashboard memory limit proxy

memories.title: Partner property ids are mapped through property_map
memories.content: Partner-specific property ids are translated to our property_id through the property_map table before an event is published. Events with unknown ids are parked until the mapping exists.
memories.keywords: property id mapping partner translate park unknown

memories.title: Register new metrics in internal/metrics with the ingest_ prefix
memories.content: New Prometheus metrics are declared in internal/metrics with promauto and the ingest_ prefix, with labels limited to partner and outcome. Tenant ids are never labels because of cardinality.
memories.keywords: prometheus metric register labels cardinality prefix

memories.title: Commit messages are one Conventional Commits subject line
memories.content: Every commit message is a single Conventional Commits subject line, type(scope): summary, with no body and no trailers. Multi-file work is split into thematic commits.
memories.keywords: commit message conventional commits subject trailer body

memories.title: No comments in code
memories.content: The user wants no comments of any kind in code; names and structure carry the meaning. Rationale goes into the pull request description or the decision log.
memories.keywords: comments docstring jsdoc code style self-documenting

memories.title: Write a failing test before changing behaviour
memories.content: Before any behaviour change, write one test and watch it fail for the intended reason. A bug fix needs a regression test that reproduces the defect first.
memories.keywords: tdd test first red green regression test

memories.title: Prefer flat early-return guards
memories.content: The user prefers flat early-return guards over nested if/else blocks. Deep nesting gets rewritten during review.
memories.keywords: early return guard clause nesting if else

memories.title: Never commit onto main, dev, develop or staging
memories.content: Never commit directly onto a shared branch such as main, dev, develop or staging. Create a branch named <type>/<TICKET>/<slug> before the first commit.
memories.value_text: ticket branch, never a shared branch
memories.keywords: branch shared main develop staging commit ticket

memories.title: Reply in the user's language; write code and docs in English
memories.content: Reply in the language the user writes in, which is often Czech, but write identifiers, commit messages, docs and stored memories in English.

memories.keywords: language czech english reply docs identifiers

memories.title: Never use any in TypeScript
memories.content: Never use any in TypeScript; accept unknown at the boundary and narrow it. Lint suppressions are not an acceptable workaround.

memories.title: Avoid adding dependencies
memories.content: Prefer the standard library and packages that are already installed. A new dependency needs a stated reason in the plan.
memories.keywords: dependency dependencies package library install add

memories.title: Edit files with the editor tools, never shell heredocs
memories.content: Make every file change with the Write and Edit tools so the user can review the diff. Never write files with heredocs, sed -i, tee or echo redirection.
memories.keywords: edit file write heredoc sed tee shell diff review

memories.title: Pull request descriptions are short and human
memories.content: Pull request descriptions are a few plain sentences about purpose and risk. Generated checklists and long summaries get deleted.
memories.keywords: pull request description pr summary checklist

memories.title: Review findings are numbered and anchored to file:line
memories.content: Report each review finding as a numbered item anchored to file:line with a short What and Why, always in English.
memories.value_text: numbered file:line with What and Why
memories.keywords: code review findings file line what why format

memories.title: Never print or store secrets
memories.content: Never echo secrets, tokens or connection strings into logs, commits, chat or memory. Refer to a secret by its variable name instead.
memories.keywords: secret token password credentials api key env leak

memories.title: The user works in the Europe/Prague timezone
memories.content: The user is based in Europe/Prague, so times such as tomorrow at 9 mean Prague time unless stated otherwise.
memories.keywords: timezone time prague cet schedule

memories.title: Update branches by rebasing; force-push only with lease
memories.content: Update a feature branch by rebasing onto its target instead of merging. Force-push only with --force-with-lease and only after the user confirms.
memories.keywords: rebase merge force push lease update branch

memories.content: When finishing a task, state which commands ran and their actual results, including failures and anything left unverified.
memories.keywords: report verification checks tests results done summary

memories.content: The user prefers named exports over default exports in TypeScript and JavaScript modules, because renames then stay consistent across imports.
memories.keywords: export named default module import typescript javascript

memories.title: Write dates as ISO 8601
memories.content: Write dates in notes, docs and file names as ISO 8601, such as 2026-10-14, never as 14.10. or 10/14.
memories.keywords: date format iso 8601 notes docs file names

memories.title: The user works on macOS with zsh and Homebrew
memories.content: The user's machine runs macOS with zsh and Homebrew, so shell snippets must work in zsh and with the BSD versions of the core tools.
memories.keywords: macos zsh homebrew shell terminal bsd tools

memories.title: Spell identifiers out
memories.content: The user wants identifiers spelled out in full, such as configuration instead of cfg or manager instead of mgr. Only universally known abbreviations like id or url are fine.
memories.keywords: naming identifiers abbreviations variable names readability

memories.title: Diagrams are Mermaid code blocks
memories.content: Diagrams in docs and design notes are Mermaid code blocks rather than images, so they can be reviewed in a diff.
memories.keywords: diagram mermaid docs image design notes

memories.title: Use pathlib in Python
memories.content: In Python the user prefers pathlib.Path over os.path string handling for every file path.
memories.keywords: python pathlib os.path file path

memories.content: Exported TypeScript functions declare an explicit return type, so a change inside the function cannot silently widen the public contract.

memories.title: Pin dependency versions exactly
memories.content: Dependency versions are pinned exactly, without ^ or ~ ranges, so two installs of the same commit resolve the same packages.

memories.title: Commits are signed with the user's SSH key
memories.content: Git signs every commit with the user's SSH key. Never pass --no-gpg-sign or turn signing off to get a commit through.
memories.keywords: commit signing ssh key gpg git

memories.title: GitHub work goes through the authenticated gh CLI
memories.content: The gh CLI is installed and authenticated, so pull requests, issues and CI logs are read with gh rather than through the web UI.

memories.title: No emoji
memories.content: The user wants no emoji in replies, docs or UI copy.
memories.keywords: emoji replies docs ui copy style

memories.title: SQL keywords in upper case, one clause per line
memories.content: Hand-written SQL uses upper-case keywords and one clause per line, with table aliases spelled out.
memories.value_text: upper-case keywords, one clause per line
memories.keywords: sql formatting keywords uppercase clause alias style

memories.title: Every new environment variable goes into .env.example
memories.content: Every new environment variable is added to .env.example with a placeholder value and a name that says what it holds.
memories.keywords: environment variable env example placeholder documentation

memories.title: Point out unrelated problems instead of fixing them
memories.content: When you notice an unrelated problem while working, point it out but do not change it without being asked.
memories.keywords: scope unrelated problem fix mention discipline

memories.title: Return new values instead of mutating
memories.content: The user prefers functions that return new values over functions that mutate their arguments or shared state.
memories.keywords: immutability mutation arguments pure functions state

memories.title: ModuleNotFoundError for billing means pytest ran outside the uv environment
memories.content: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'billing'` while pytest collects the suite means it ran on the system Python instead of the project environment. Run `uv run pytest -q`; never set PYTHONPATH or pip install the package to get around it.

memories.title: SignatureVerificationError on a Stripe webhook: verify the raw body with this endpoint's secret
memories.content: `SignatureVerificationError: No signatures found matching the expected signature` comes from verifying a re-serialised JSON body or another endpoint's signing secret. Pass `await request.body()` unchanged to `stripe.Webhook.construct_event` with the `whsec_` secret of this endpoint; tests sign payloads with the WebhookSignature helper.

memories.content: A duplicate key on `invoices_number_key` means two workers numbered invoices concurrently. Numbers come only from `next_invoice_number()` inside the advisory lock; tests that finalize invoices under xdist use the numbering fixture.

memories.keywords: duplicate key invoice number unique constraint invoices_number_key advisory lock xdist

memories.title: ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE: run pnpm install locally and commit pnpm-lock.yaml
memories.content: CI installs with `--frozen-lockfile`, so a package.json change without the matching pnpm-lock.yaml fails with ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE. Run `pnpm install` locally and commit the updated lockfile in the same commit; never pass `--no-frozen-lockfile` in CI.

memories.content: `src/api/generated/` is not committed. After a fresh clone or a backend schema change, `error TS2307: Cannot find module '@/api/generated/client'` means the client was not generated yet: run `pnpm api:generate`.

memories.title: Playwright browser executable missing: run pnpm exec playwright install chromium
memories.content: `browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist` under ms-playwright after a Playwright upgrade means the browsers of the new version are not downloaded. Run `pnpm exec playwright install chromium`; CI caches them per Playwright version.

memories.title: MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED on a ClickHouse insert: lower the sink batch size
memories.content: ClickHouse code 241 MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED during a sink flush means the batch is too large for the per-query limit. Lower SINK_MAX_BATCH_ROWS (default 50 000) instead of raising max_memory_usage, which the dashboards share.

memories.title: UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PARTITION locally: create the topics with make topics
memories.content: Topic auto-creation is off in Redpanda and in production, so a consumer started against a fresh local broker fails with UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PARTITION. Run `make topics` after `docker compose up`; production topics come from the Helm chart.

memories.content: ClickHouse code 252 TOO_MANY_PARTS means inserts arrive faster than merges, usually from per-event inserts in a replay or backfill. Send every insert through the sink batcher (at least 10 000 rows or 1 s per insert); never insert row by row.
